lead: A `python - <<'PY'` heredoc mangles non-ASCII in the *matched* string, so a `str.replace` on a `§` or an em dash finds nothing.
body: Writing one out is fine; an `assert s.count(old) == 1` over a fragment quoted from a doc comment fails with no clue why, and re-grepping the file only confirms the text *is* there. Use Edit for anything whose anchor is prose; a heredoc is safe only when every matched byte is ASCII.
